outcome: Fetal complications (respiratory distress, meconium aspiration syndrome)
cohort: 1306 women with singleton pregnancies who underwent cesarean section at a tertiary referral center over one year.
finding: Fetal complications, including respiratory distress, meconium aspiration syndrome, and NICU admissions >24 hours, were significantly higher in the emergency cesarean section group compared to the elective group.
gest_age: Not specified (study included patients regardless of gestational age)
birth_weight: Mean birth weight was significantly higher in the elective group (2.58 kg) compared to the emergency group (2.43 kg).
